thread:
zoe: small but annoying: generated client methods lose arg name typing when we use **kwargs forwarding in wrapper helpers. pyright flags `unexpected keyword argument` in some sample apps.

mat: ugh that was a shortcut in autogen to avoid enumerating repeated params in wrappers. The stub ends up as `def create_foo(**kwargs: Any) -> Foo` which is bad.

hana: big UX hit for newcomers. sample-apps call create_foo(title="x") and pyright yells even though runtime accepts it.

zoe: quick fix is to generate explicit signatures in wrappers, or use `def create_foo(*, title: str | None = None, ...) -> Foo` in stubs. Runtime can still forward kwargs, but stubs should be precise.

mat: will update the autogen to expand common params into wrapper stubs. smaller surface than other fixes.

dev-bot: created issue #2401 "stub: preserve explicit param names in wrapper methods instead of **kwargs: Any"

zoe: thanks — will update onboarding note about `# type: ignore` workarounds until this ships.
